title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: SiteMinder Person
tiers.description: All Directors and Senior Management (each director, the CEO, CFO, Managing Director and Company Secretary, Key Management Personnel) and any other person the Board designates in writing, plus a company or trust controlled by any of them (at all times), plus (for section 4 purposes only) their spouse, child, close relative, financial dependant or person acting in concert with them.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The chair of the Board; distinguished only as a distinct authorising-officer category (approved by the Audit and Risk Committee chair plus one other director).

tiers.name: Other directors, Company Secretary and any other Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chair, the Company Secretary, and any other KMP; distinguished only for the authorising-officer table (Board chair, or Audit and Risk Committee chair in the Board chair's absence, plus one other director).

tiers.name: Any other SiteMinder Person
tiers.description: SiteMinder Persons who are not directors, the Company Secretary or KMP (i.e. other designated persons); distinguished only for the authorising-officer table (Company Secretary, or CEO in the Company Secretary's absence).

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A company or trust controlled by a SiteMinder Person (a SiteMinder Person for all purposes), and, for section 4 (Blackout Periods and consent) purposes only, a spouse (including de facto), child (including step-child or adopted child), close relative, person financially dependent on, or person acting in concert with, a SiteMinder Person.

definitions.hedging_definition: Operate to limit the economic risk of any SiteMinder Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including SiteMinder's securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under any SiteMinder incentive plan) on that SiteMinder Person's behalf

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of SiteMinder securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of collared shares under the loan is a policy-exempt dealing rather than a breach, even during a Blackout Period, though the executive must still advise the relevant Authorising Officer(s) afterwards.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Otherwise enable a SiteMinder Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The catch-all wording is broad enough to capture the purchased-put leg of a collar (which profits on a price fall) even if it is not badged as a hedge, reinforcing that clearance (or an outright ban if unvested/locked) applies to that leg.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a company or trust controlled by any of the persons referred to in sub-paragraph (i) above
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike natural-person associates (caught only for section 4 purposes), a controlled company or trust is a SiteMinder Person for all purposes, so routing the collar or loan through a family entity does not avoid the section 5.2/5.3 bans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Chair of the Board: The chair of the Audit and Risk Committee and one other Board director. Other directors, Company Secretary and any other Key Management Personnel: The chair of the Board or, in his/her absence, the chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, and one other Board Director.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Director/KMP clearance for the collar's derivative and security-granting legs needs two named approvers rather than one, which can add time to structuring and requires both to accept the 10-business-day execution window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy will be regarded seriously and may lead to disciplinary action, including dismissal.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside the narrow hardship/court-order exceptional-circumstances route, there is no standing waiver mechanism for the policy's bans on unvested/locked hedging and secured financing, so a funded collar over such shares cannot be cleared by consent alone.

summary: A funded collar is possible over vested, lock-free SiteMinder shares but not over unvested or holding-locked shares. Section 5.2 treats a protection arrangement (which functionally captures an OTC put/call or monetisation) over unvested or holding-locked securities as banned outright, and section 5.3 imposes the same absolute ban on granting security (including a collateral loan) over such shares; both restrictions convert to a permitted-with-consent regime once the shares vest and any holding lock lifts. Consent under section 4.2 must come from two named Authorising Officers (varying by tier), the trade must complete within 10 business days of consent, cannot occur during a Blackout Period (half-year, full-year and AGM windows) or while holding inside information, and any security granted must be notified promptly to the Company Secretary. A forced sale on the bank's enforcement of the loan is an exempt dealing even in a Blackout Period, but there is no general hardship-style waiver for the underlying vesting/holding-lock bans, so the collar's timing depends on the shares' vesting and lock status rather than lender discretion.
